methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study with 465 patients, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, and appropriate statistical methods (ROC, Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression). Excellent imaging reliability demonstrated (ICC 0.943-0.951). However, lacks pre-specified primary outcome, power calculation, and multiplicity correction. Single-center design and acknowledged retrospective bias limit generalizability.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study evaluating standardized splenic volume and lymphocyte percentage as prognostic biomarkers in UTUC post-nephroureterectomy. Findings propose actionable risk stratification tool using accessible imaging and laboratory parameters. Clinical relevance is plausible but requires external validation before clinical implementation; not yet practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational study with adequate STROBE adherence: clear methods, results with confidence intervals, and comprehensive discussion. Most key reporting items present including study design diagram (Fig. 1A), statistical methods, and multivariable analysis. Gaps include limited reporting of confounder adjustment details and no data availability statement. No mention of public data access or repository deposition.

novelty_literature.justification: First systematic evaluation of splenic volume in upper tract urothelial carcinoma, extending prior work demonstrating splenomegaly association in HCC, colorectal, lung, and pancreatic cancers. Meaningful contribution through dual biomarker integration (SV + lym%) and application to understudied disease area. Fills documented gap in UTUC biomarker literature but represents incremental methodological extension rather than novel mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear abstract, introduction, methods, and results sections. Effective use of tables (clinical characteristics, univariate/multivariate analyses) and figures (Kaplan-Meier curves, correlation plots). Discussion section is comprehensive though somewhat dense. Overall publication-ready clarity with minor opportunities for tightening in discussion synthesis.

key_strengths: Novel application of standardized splenic volume to UTUC with excellent imaging reliability (ICC >0.94)
Integrated biomarker approach combining accessible imaging and routine laboratory parameters for risk stratification
Comprehensive survival analysis across three endpoints (OS, CSS, MFS) with multivariate adjustment for key clinicopathological factors
Clear mechanistic rationale grounded in preclinical evidence of immune dysregulation and MDSC expansion
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with acknowledged selection bias and limited generalizability requiring external validation
ROC-derived cutoffs (79 cm3/m2, 21%) lack biological justification and external validation; modest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.526-0.630)
No pre-specified primary outcome, power calculation, or multiplicity correction; no longitudinal immune profiling to demonstrate mechanism
Complete absence of data availability statement; no plan for reproducibility or sharing of imaging/clinical data
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid incremental contribution with competent methodology and clear clinical application pathway, appropriate for Tier 3 venues (Cancers, European J Cancer, BMC Cancer). Requires external cohort validation and extended mechanistic evaluation before higher-tier consideration.
